newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela keeps lid on spending despite pay rises.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela keeps lid on spending despite pay rises.

text.p: The Venezuelan government aims to keep public spending at the same real levels as last year despite an improved pay offer to the country's 1.2 million bureaucrats, a top government official said Thursday.
"The official proposal is to keep the level of spending at the same level as in 1996 as a percentage of gross domestic product," the official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.
This level is between 3.5 and four percent of GDP, he said.

Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar announced Wednesday that the government had improved its pay offer to public sector workers to 35 percent from an original 25 percent. The government also offered a 50 percent increase in monthly bonuses.
Government officials say the new pay offer will not have an adverse impact on inflation targets of 25 to 30 percent.
"The proposal is manageable up to this level because it is within the limit of public spending set aside for this year," the government official said.
With the new pay offer, total government spending on wages rises to 1.25 trillion bolivars ($2.6 billion), up from 900 billion bolivars ($1.9 billion) orginally set aside.
"What is clear is that this (the extra spending) cannot be covered with more borrowing nor exclusively through oil revenues," the government source said.
